To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

using the experimental– theoretical method and physical criteria for the data reliability, cross section of partial photoneutrn reactions (γ,1n), ( γ, 2n), (γ 3n) are obtained for 186W and 141Pr nuclei.
using the ETM, the cross sections of partial reactions (γ, in) are obtained for 1 ≤ i ≤ 3 at energies up to 21 and 22 MeV for 141Pr, 186W, respectively.

using the experimental-theoretical method (ETMs), the cross sections of partial (γ, 0n), (γ,1n), ( γ,2n), ( γ, 3n), (γ n) photoneutron reactions were obtained for 141 Pr and 186 W nuclei, and it was shown that at the same energies, the experimental distribution of neutros in channels with multiplicities of 1, 3 and 4 is not reliable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of data reliability in the analysis of experimental results of photonuclear reactions.

the development of the ETM for obtaining reliable cross sections of partial photonuclear reactions and with a study of the reliability of the experimental neutron multiplicity sorting data for the (γ, n), (γ, xn) and (γp, n) reactions on the basis of the ETM.
a new method for the analysis of experimental neutron multiplicity spectra and a method for evaluating the cross sections of partial photonuclear reactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ETM is a method that can be recommended for the estimation of partial photoneutrons reaction cross sections, but it is not a method that can provide reliable data on these cross sections.
the ETM method is not suitable for estimating the cross section of partial photoneutrons for 141Pr, and the cross section is evaluated only for 186W.
, at least in some cases, the neutron multiplicity sorting method used in the experiment on beams of quasicommon-energy photons is not sufficiently reliable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in order to obtain the reliable cross sections of partial reactions (γ, xn) for 141Pr, 186W, 197Au, 209Bi, and 232Th nuclei, the experimental–theoretica method should be used at photon energies up to 21–25 MeV.
, in the case of the 141Pr and W nuclei, it is not possible to evaluate the cross sections of partial reactions (γ, xn) from the experimental cross section σexp(γ,nxn).
the cross sections of partial reactions (γ, xn) are not reliably obtained by sorting the neutrons in the beam by multiplicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ETM can be used for evaluating cross sections of partial photonuclear reactions only if the data reliability criteria are met.
it is necessary to take into account the experimental data reliability criteria when evaluating the photoneutron cross sections.
the experimental–theological approach to estimating the cross sections of partial reactions is not applicable to the nuclei with Z ≥ 57.
